speed.what: How fast the character moves, in meters per second.
speed.typical: 2.0 sneaking / 5.0 normal walk / 8.0 action game / 15.0+ sprint
speed.increase: Above 12 feels arcadey, hard to steer precisely.
speed.decrease: Below 3 feels sluggish for most 3D games.

details.what: A CharacterBody3D that reads WASD input and moves on the XZ plane.
details.where: Attach to a CharacterBody3D. Add a CollisionShape3D child or the character falls through the floor.
details.before: Create input actions: left, right, forward, back in Project Settings > Input Map.
details.after: Add a Camera3D as a child. For mouse look, also insert 'mouse look 3d'.
details.why_optimized: Uses @export for editor tuning, Input.get_vector for analog input, no per-frame allocations.
details.mistakes: Forgetting move_and_slide() means no movement. Forgetting CollisionShape3D means falling through the world.

speed.what: Horizontal run speed, in pixels per second.
speed.typical: 100 slow walk / 200 normal / 350 fast / 500+ speedrun feel
speed.increase: Feels snappier but harder to land precise jumps.

jump_velocity.what: Upward push applied at jump start. Negative is up in 2D.
jump_velocity.increase: More negative = higher jump. Goes higher, stays in air longer.
jump_velocity.decrease: Less negative = shorter jump. Below -200 barely hops.

gravity.what: Downward acceleration, in pixels per second squared.
gravity.increase: Faster fall, more weight. Pairs well with high jump_velocity.

details.what: A 2D platformer character with gravity, jumping, and left/right movement.
details.where: Attach to a CharacterBody2D. Add a CollisionShape2D child.
details.before: Create input actions: left, right, jump in Project Settings > Input Map.
details.after: Build a floor with StaticBody2D + CollisionShape2D so is_on_floor() returns true.
details.why_optimized: Input.is_action_just_pressed prevents double-jump. get_axis returns smooth analog input.
details.mistakes: Using is_action_pressed for jump causes repeated jumps. Forgetting move_and_slide() means no movement.

jump_velocity.what: Upward impulse applied when jump is pressed. Positive is up in 3D.
jump_velocity.increase: Higher jump, longer air time. Above 12 you'll clear most level geometry.
jump_velocity.decrease: Lower jump. Below 2.0 barely lifts off the ground.

details.what: Adds gravity and a jump impulse to a CharacterBody3D.
details.where: Meant to be inside a CharacterBody3D's script. Assumes gravity is Godot's default.
details.before: Create the input action 'jump' in Project Settings > Input Map (usually bound to Space).
details.after: Tune jump_velocity by feel. Pair with a sprint snippet if you want run+jump.
details.why_optimized: get_gravity() uses the project's gravity setting instead of a hardcoded value.
details.mistakes: Using velocity.y = 4.5 instead of += means you overwrite gravity every frame.

heal.code:
func heal(amount: int) -> void:
	health = min(health + amount, max_health)

die.code:
signal died

func die() -> void:
	died.emit()
	queue_free()

state_machine.code:
enum State { IDLE, WALK, ATTACK }

var state: State = State.IDLE

func _set_state(new_state: State) -> void:
	if state == new_state:
		return
	_exit_state(state)
	state = new_state
	_enter_state(state)

func _enter_state(s: State) -> void:
	match s:
		State.IDLE:
			pass
		State.WALK:
			pass
		State.ATTACK:
			pass

func _exit_state(_s: State) -> void:
	pass

item_pickup_signal.code:
signal item_picked(item_id: String)

func pickup(item_id: String) -> void:
	item_picked.emit(item_id)
	queue_free()

score_display.code:
extends Label

var score: int = 0

func add_score(amount: int) -> void:
	score += amount
	text = "Score: %d" % score

details.what: A CanvasLayer that pauses the game and shows/hides a menu when Escape is pressed.
details.where: Attach to a CanvasLayer. Add a Panel or ColorRect as a child so it actually covers the screen.
details.before: Nothing required. ui_cancel is Godot's built-in Escape action.
details.after: Add Button nodes as children for Resume / Restart / Quit. Connect their pressed signals.
details.why_optimized: Uses process_mode = ALWAYS so the menu keeps working while the game is paused.
details.mistakes: Forgetting process_mode = ALWAYS means the pause menu itself is frozen and can't unpause.

pause_game.code:
func toggle_pause() -> void:
	get_tree().paused = not get_tree().paused

timer.code:
func delayed_call(delay: float, callback: Callable) -> void:
	get_tree().create_timer(delay).timeout.connect(callback)

await_timer.code:
func wait(seconds: float) -> void:
	await get_tree().create_timer(seconds).timeout

ray_length.what: How far the ray reaches before giving up, in meters.
ray_length.typical: 5 short interaction / 100 gun range / 1000+ long sight line
ray_length.increase: Sees further. Costs nothing extra — the ray just tests more distance.
ray_length.decrease: Shorter reach. Useful for interaction prompts and melee range.

details.what: Casts a ray from a point in a direction and returns what it hits.
details.where: Put on any Node3D that has access to the 3D world (not a CanvasLayer or pure UI node).
details.after: Check the returned Dictionary for 'collider' — that's the object the ray hit.
details.why_optimized: Uses direct_space_state instead of a RayCast3D node — no scene-tree overhead per cast.
details.mistakes: Forgetting that an empty Dictionary means nothing was hit. Forgetting to update 'from' if the caster moves.

player_3d.title: 3D Character
setup_notes: The CollisionShape3D has a CapsuleShape3D placeholder. Select it and adjust the height/radius to match your character.
The Body node has a BoxMesh placeholder. Replace it with your actual mesh (.glb or .obj) by dragging it onto the Body node.
The Camera3D is a placeholder. For first-person you'd delete it and use 'first person camera'. For third-person, use 'camera follow 3d'.

next_steps.why: So the player has something to stand on.
To look around with the mouse.
Add jumping to the movement script.
So you can pause the game.

mistakes: Forgetting CollisionShape3D means the player falls through the floor.
Attaching the script to the Camera3D instead of the CharacterBody3D means nothing moves.
Making the CapsuleShape3D too small means the player clips into walls.

player_2d_platformer.title: 2D Platformer Character
setup_notes: Drag your character sprite onto the Sprite node.
Adjust the CollisionShape2D rectangle to roughly match your sprite bounds.

next_steps.why: Makes jumping feel fair when you just walk off a ledge.
Lets a jump pressed slightly early still register.
So the camera tracks the player.

mistakes: Forgetting move_and_slide() means nothing happens on screen.
Using a square CollisionShape2D for a round character means visible gaps.

ground_plane_3d.title: Ground Plane (3D)
setup_notes: The PlaneMesh defaults to 2x2 meters. In the Inspector, set its size to something large like 50x50.
The BoxShape3D needs to be thin and wide — set its size to (50, 0.2, 50) to match.
To color the ground, add a StandardMaterial3D to the MeshInstance3D's material slot.

next_steps.why: The player needs somewhere to stand.

mistakes: Forgetting the CollisionShape3D means the player falls through the ground.
Making the mesh bigger than the collision shape means parts of the floor are ghostly.

pause_menu_ui.title: Pause Menu
setup_notes: Add Button nodes as children of the Buttons VBoxContainer.
Name them Resume, Restart, Quit — the script only handles opening/closing.

next_steps.why: For the pause menu's Quit button to return to.

mistakes: Forgetting process_mode = ALWAYS means the menu itself freezes.
The script is on CanvasLayer — attaching it to a Button instead breaks everything.

enemy_patrol_2d.title: Patrolling Enemy (2D)
setup_notes: In the Inspector, fill the 'points' array with Vector2 world positions the enemy should walk between.
Drag your enemy sprite onto the Sprite node.

next_steps.why: So the enemy can notice the player.
So the enemy can chase once it sees the player.
So the enemy can deal damage.

mistakes: Forgetting to set patrol points means the enemy stands still.
Making the enemy's collision shape too large means it gets stuck on corners.
